item.content:encoded:
Astronomers warn SpaceX’s million AI satellites threaten research

Category: AI

Astronomy organizations warn that SpaceX’s proposed network of AI-computing satellites could disrupt scientific observations after the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) authorized up to 1 million Starmind spacecraft on Nov. 25. The American Astronomical Society said the satellites could be brighter and more numerous than existing objects, remain visible longer, and produce radio emissions and waste heat that could affect sensitive instruments [2][1]. Starmind would use computing hardware on solar-powered satellites to process AI workloads in orbit, then send results to Earth through SpaceX’s satellite network. The plan aims to meet AI’s demand for more computing capacity, but experts cite unresolved challenges in removing heat in a vacuum and moving large volumes of data. SpaceX warned in a regulatory filing that the technologies were unproven and might not be commercially viable [15][13][2]. A European Southern Observatory simulation estimated that satellite trails could obscure up to 28% of images captured by its Very Large Telescope in Chile under specified conditions, even if SpaceX substantially dims its satellites [5]. The FCC authorization sets deployment deadlines through 2040, requiring an operational satellite by November 2033 [2][4].

— Prof. Sir Martin Sweeting, founder and executive chairman of Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd (BBC News)

Key Points

  • Environmental risks: Launches and reentries could pollute the atmosphere, while in-orbit collisions could create debris clouds that threaten other satellites [1].
  • Collision risks: SpaceX can maneuver functioning satellites to avoid potential collisions, but failed satellites cannot maneuver and could pose a danger in orbit [56].
  • Other projects: Blue Origin has asked the FCC to approve up to 51,600 satellites for Project Sunrise [33].
  • Orbit design: The FCC order places the satellites in orbital shells between 500 and 1,002 kilometers, with 30-degree and sun-synchronous inclinations [42].
  • Strategic control: An expert raised concerns that one entity would control a capability of this scale and that it could become a target for malicious actors [53].
  • Earth-side pressure: A Data Center Watch tally cited by ZME Science said local opposition delayed or derailed at least 120 U.S. data-center projects worth $198 billion in the first half of 2026 [5].
  • Observatory disruption: A simulation by European Southern Observatory astronomer Olivier Hainaut estimated that hundreds or thousands of satellites could be visible at once, rivaling the number of stars visible under pristine conditions [5].
  • Launch dependency: SpaceX’s deployment plan depends heavily on lower launch costs from Starship, its reusable next-generation rocket, which is still under development [4].
  • Instrument interference: The American Astronomical Society warned that radio emissions and infrared waste heat from the satellites could threaten sensitive instruments used in astronomy [37].
  • Communications: FCC approval allows radio-frequency links as a backup for telemetry, tracking and command if the satellites’ optical links fail [42].
  • Orbital disposal condition: The FCC approved SpaceX’s debris plan only for satellites below 600 kilometers; the company must submit a final disposal plan before deploying satellites in higher orbits [3].
  • Visible objects: Astronomer Michael Brown says each proposed satellite would be about 75 metres wide and brighter than any star in the early evening [56].
  • Satellite scale: SpaceX’s proposed AI1 spacecraft is designed with a wingspan of nearly 230 feet [33].
  • Existing traffic: About 17,000 satellites were already in orbit when the FCC approved the plan [24][37].

Perspectives

American Astronomical Society: The society said the FCC’s approval could compromise decades of federal investment in astronomy and people’s ability to study the night sky; it had urged the agency to reject the application [2][1].

European Southern Observatory: Director General Andreas Kaufer called for international mechanisms to assess satellite projects whose effects cross national borders, citing the observatory’s technical analysis of the proposed constellation [23].

Sources: Leonard David

Federal Communications Commission: The commission said it would not impose additional protections for optical astronomy, which it considers outside its radio-frequency remit, and accepted SpaceX’s commitment to coordinate with the National Science Foundation [3].

Amazon Leo: Amazon’s satellite unit challenged the project’s feasibility, describing it as “an ambitious dream, not a real plan,” and argued SpaceX was unlikely to deploy the full fleet [13][4].

Sources: BBC News

American Astronomical Society: The society had urged the FCC to deny SpaceX’s application before the authorization [32].

Sources: NPR

Adam Becker, astrophysicist and author: Becker called the proposal a fantasy and said it would not happen [32].

Sources: NPR

Sir Martin Sweeting, Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd: Sweeting said the concept may be technically feasible but questioned whether it makes sense at scale [13].

Sources: BBC News

Federal Communications Commission: The FCC said approval serves the public interest by allowing SpaceX to pioneer technology intended to advance U.S. leadership in space and artificial intelligence [11].

Sources: Al-Ahram

Amazon: The rival company criticized Starmind as “a lofty ambition rather than a real plan” [13].

Sources: BBC News

Federal Communications Commission: The commission said deploying the satellites serves the public interest, despite public comments and petitions asking it to deny SpaceX’s request [52].

Sources: PBS NewsHour

SpaceX: The company told the FCC that near-constant solar power and low operating costs could reduce the environmental impact of computing compared with terrestrial data centers [37].

Sources: KSL.com

Timeline

  • 25 November 2026: FCC authorized SpaceX’s proposed Starmind satellite network [15][2]
  • 2027: SpaceX has said it hopes to launch its first Starmind satellite [5][13]
  • November 2033: FCC license requires SpaceX to begin deployment no later than this month [2][4]
  • November 2035: SpaceX must have deployed 100,000 satellites under its license [2][4]
  • November 2038: License milestone requires deployment of half the authorized constellation [2][4]
  • November 2040: SpaceX must complete deployment of the authorized constellation by this deadline [4][5]
  • 30 January 2026: SpaceX filed its application for the Starmind satellite constellation [42].
  • October 2026: Google’s Project Suncatcher prototype entered orbit for testing [33].
  • 25 November 2026: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites [3].
  • 2027: SpaceX has said it aims to begin launching its first Starmind satellites [13].
  • November 2033: The FCC license requires SpaceX to have one operational satellite in orbit [35].
  • January 2026: SpaceX filed its application for up to one million computing satellites [7]
  • 25 November 2026: FCC authorized Starmind and established staged deployment requirements [3]
  • November 2033: SpaceX must place its first authorized satellite into its assigned orbit [3]
  • November 2035: SpaceX must have deployed 100,000 satellites, 10% of the maximum [3]
  • November 2038: SpaceX must have deployed 500,000 satellites, half the approved maximum [3]
  • November 2040: Deadline for SpaceX to place the full authorized constellation in orbit [3]

Technical Details

  • Thermal radiation: In orbit, air cannot carry heat away from processors; the proposed satellites would have to release waste heat as infrared radiation through radiators [15][9].
  • Hardware reliability: Unlike terrestrial servers, orbital processors are difficult to repair or replace. Technical challenges outlined for Starmind include the need for radiation protection and fault-tolerant hardware [9].
  • Distributed computing clusters: SpaceX executive Michael Nicholls described clusters of roughly 10 satellites linked at about 10 terabits per second, with connections to Starlink and the wider constellation [42].
  • Compute payload: SpaceX’s proposed payload is rated for roughly 175 kilowatts of average computing power and up to 250 kilowatts at peak; these are design specifications, not demonstrated operating results [9].
  • Payload power: SpaceX’s planned AI1 satellite is rated to provide its computing hardware with 120 kilowatts of sustained power and 150 kilowatts at peak [33].
  • Instrument risks: The American Astronomical Society also cited radio emissions and waste heat as threats to sensitive instruments used in astronomy research [37].

Scientific Significance

  • Disposal requirements: The FCC has not approved SpaceX’s proposal to send retired satellites into solar orbit and requires a final debris plan before deployment above 600 kilometers [33].
  • Atmospheric uncertainty: Scientists have raised concerns that repeated satellite burn-ups could deposit metals in the upper atmosphere, including aluminium compounds that researchers have linked to ozone destruction. The projected scale depends on the satellites’ eventual operating lifespan and replacement rate [56][53].
  • Hardware resilience: Experts identify processors’ ability to withstand space radiation and micrometeorite impacts as unresolved obstacles [30].
  • Proposed limit: Hainaut recommended limiting the total satellite population to approximately 100,000 sufficiently dim satellites to protect astronomical observations [5].
  • Environmental effects: Critics also cited atmospheric pollution from satellite launches and reentries as a potential concern [32].

Historical Background

Satellite operators sometimes seek approval for more satellites than they ultimately intend to deploy to preserve flexibility in their network designs. SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites, while just over 11,000 are now in orbit [4][24].

Q&A

Q: Does approval mean SpaceX will launch all one million satellites?

A: Not necessarily. Operators may request approval for more satellites than they intend to deploy. SpaceX sought clearance for 42,000 Starlink satellites and has put just over 11,000 in orbit [24].

Q: What disposal review remains before some Starmind satellites can be deployed?

A: The FCC deferred SpaceX’s proposal to place retired satellites in solar orbit and requires a final debris plan before deployment above 600 kilometers [33].

Q: Why could the highest satellite orbits raise disposal concerns?

A: The FCC approved disposal planning for satellites below 600 kilometers but deferred deployment in higher orbits until SpaceX submits a final disposal plan. The company had not supplied enough information for the FCC to assess its proposed methods [3].

Anthropic co-founders disclosed $560 million in pre-IPO share sales

Category: AI

Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei, the chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, the company’s president and board chair, each sold 3.3784 million shares at the $83 initial public offering price, worth about $560 million combined, according to filings cited by BigGo [6]. Shares in the Claude developer closed at $82.79 on Nov. 25, below the offer price five trading sessions after its record $81.3 billion IPO [11][12]. Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue reached $16.96 billion, up from $1.38 billion a year earlier, while the company recorded a $567 million operating loss [10]. Computing and infrastructure expenses rose $4.3 billion in the quarter as revenue increased $5.4 billion from the previous quarter [10]. The company has roughly $900 billion in long-term computing and infrastructure commitments and faces a series of share lockup expirations. Up to 303 million shares could become eligible for sale on Dec. 15, and Anthropic is expected to release its first results as a public company early next year [10][12][6].

It seems that these companies are trying to one-up each other on the amount of money that they're spending, but you have to show that it's worth it, and that's where Wall Street is saying 'I don't know'

— Todd Schoenberger, chief investment officer at CrossCheck Management (Reuters, republished by Zawya)

Key Points

  • Customer growth: The number of Anthropic customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue rose from more than 950 to over 11,900 in a year; more than 1,900 customers were spending at least $1 million annually by the third quarter [10].
  • Usage-based sales: About 79% of Anthropic’s revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came from usage-based charges, leaving sales exposed if customers reduce token consumption or switch to cheaper models [10].
  • Discount pressure: Price cuts and customer discounts introduced in the second and third quarters reduced revenue by about $600 million, as Anthropic competed with ChatGPT, Gemini and other models [10][17].
  • IPO float: About 11% of Anthropic’s shares were freely tradable at listing, compared with less than 5% in SpaceX’s IPO, according to BigGo’s comparison [6].
  • Sector strain: The Nov. 26 selloff also hit major AI-linked firms: Nvidia fell 8.5%, while CoreWeave and Nebius each dropped more than 10% [15].

Perspectives

Chris Beauchamp, IG Group’s chief market analyst, said attention after an IPO typically shifts from hype to scrutiny of financial performance, growth prospects and valuation [6].

Sources: BigGo Finance

Tom Hulick, chief executive of Strategy Asset Managers, said investors should wait for reported results to confirm performance, describing Anthropic as a test case for the AI capital-spending cycle [6].

Sources: BigGo Finance

Timeline

  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic began Nasdaq trading after pricing shares at $83 [11][5]
  • 24 November 2026: Shares closed below their IPO price for the first time [6][12]
  • 25 November 2026: Shares ended at $82.79, below the IPO price for a second session [11]
  • 15 December 2026: Up to 303 million shares may become eligible for sale [12][8]

Industry Impact

  • Anthropic’s adjusted operating margin fell from 19% in the second quarter to 15% in the third, mainly due to $5 billion in costs associated with short-term computing-capacity deals [10].

SAP targets product and engineering teams in AI overhaul

Category: AI

SAP has asked teams in product development, engineering and sales to identify potential reductions as it reorganizes its enterprise software business around artificial intelligence. People familiar with the discussions said earlier attempts to introduce AI products faced problems [2][13]. The plan under consideration would eliminate at least 10,000 jobs, but the final figure could change after labor negotiations [2][1]. At a May user conference, SAP introduced Joule Work, an interface intended to give employees a single point of access to its applications, along with Joule Assistants and Industry AI for sector-specific workflows [3]. SAP said its assistants would use more than 200 subagents to automate repetitive business tasks [3]. SAP has not confirmed the proposed cuts [2]. In the United States, employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, about 20% of the total, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas [5]. SAP is expected to provide more detail with its full-year results in January [9].

Companies are spending billions of dollars on AI infrastructure, software and talent. At the same time, many are trimming roles viewed as overlapping, manual or less critical to future growth

— Krishna Iyer, corporate governance expert (NDTV)

Key Points

  • AI investments: SAP completed four acquisitions in 2026—Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf—and made strategic investments in AI-focused firms Parloa, n8n and Conduct [5].
  • Previous overhaul: SAP’s 2024 restructuring relied mainly on voluntary departures and retraining; hiring for new roles kept overall headcount relatively flat [10].
  • German protections: An agreement negotiated by SAP’s German employee representatives protects employment through 2028 and provides alternative roles, training and preserved salary levels for affected employees [4].
  • Leadership changes: Two of SAP’s six executive board members are due to leave in March. Chief Executive Christian Klein took over most of product lead Muhammad Alam’s duties, while sales chief Thomas Saueressig plans to leave for Ionos [10].

Perspectives

SAP: The company said it regularly reviews its organization to keep it aligned with its strategy and customer needs. It declined to confirm whether cuts are planned [2].

item.content:encoded:
AI shopping assistants reshape Black Friday as scams and errors rise

Category: AI

Consumers are using artificial intelligence chatbots to compare prices and find gift ideas, while newer AI agents can browse stores, track deliveries and make purchases. The U.S. National Retail Federation says 59% of consumers plan to use AI for holiday shopping; Black Friday is Nov. 27, followed by Cyber Monday on Nov. 30 [7][16]. In Australia, a separate survey found one in four shoppers planned to use an AI chatbot for research, and 72% of that group said it would be their first time [17]. Chatbots can invent products or prices, recommend unsuitable items and expose data shared to personalize results. Visa testing found AI models failed to recommend a product matching a customer’s needs in 42% of test runs, while cybersecurity experts warn that malicious website instructions can manipulate agents with access to email or payment details [7][8]. Retailers are also using AI to set discounts and influence which products shoppers see. Adobe data cited by retailers showed traffic to online shops from AI-tool links more than doubled this November from a year earlier, while marketing teams are adjusting product listings to appear in chat recommendations [5][3].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

You should always think about AI as a black box, right? We don’t necessarily know where the data you’re putting in is going to end up.

— Bryan Carr, chair of information sciences at the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay (WBAY)

Key Points

  • Accuracy gap: A survey by online-reputation company Custplace found AI gave incorrect product answers 64% of the time, with fluctuating prices a frequent source of mistakes [18].
  • Retail discounts: Salesforce said November discounts before Black Friday averaged 8% deeper than a year earlier, while Adobe expected TV discounts to average 23% on Black Friday versus 11% earlier in the month [5].
  • Data exposure: TrendLife data showed 76% of Australians already using AI agents had granted access to personal accounts or data, and 15% were willing to let agents complete purchases [8].
  • Shopping patterns: Adobe reported online sales of personal-hygiene goods from Nov. 1-22 were 40% above October’s average, while cleaning products rose 33% and clothing basics 27% [5].
  • Consumer losses: Australia’s Scamwatch recorded $22.2 million in losses from buying-and-selling scams during 2026, as authorities warned criminals may exploit AI shopping agents [8].

Perspectives

Meta: Meta says Muse assigns each user a separate agent, keeps information private and stores sensitive details such as credit-card numbers separately from the AI.

Sources: GPB

David Schweidel, Emory University Goizueta Business School professor: Schweidel warned that shoppers may compete with automated bots able to snap up high-demand deals in seconds, likening the situation to ticket-buying bots.

Sources: FOX 5 Atlanta

Timeline

  • 2022: Meta settled a case over user-data sharing for about $725 million [7]
  • November 2026: Meta’s Muse shopping agent launched in Australia the previous week [17]
  • 27 November 2026: Black Friday began [16]
  • 30 November 2026: Cyber Monday will follow the Black Friday sales period [16]

Industry Impact

  • Retail cybersecurity: Ransomware attacks on retailers are 50% more frequent in November, Semafor reported, and the sector has low levels of cyber insurance [10].

Q&A

Q: Why are some retailers blocking outside shopping agents?

A: Amazon says Meta did not notify it before Muse began browsing and that the agents did not identify themselves; Amazon also operates its own shopping agent [7][17].

Q: How can shoppers tell whether a sale price is genuine?

A: Greek consumer guidance says the displayed reference price should be the product’s lowest price in the previous 30 days [16].

Action Items

  • Be specific about intended use and constraints—for example, ask whether a bag will fit under an airplane seat—rather than expecting a vague prompt to capture your needs [7].
  • Avoid sharing identifying details about friends or relatives when brainstorming gifts; AI systems may use those details to build profiles of people you shop for [7].
  • Check independent reviews and the seller’s return policy, including where items must be shipped and who pays return shipping, before placing an order [1].

item.title: Governments and AI leaders press for human oversight as safety rules diverge
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (AI / Ai Safety)
item.description: Governments and technology leaders are pursuing AI safety measures ranging from voluntary international commitments to proposed inspections and mandatory incident reporting. The Paris Call, signed Nov. 9 by governments, AI companies and civil-society groups, is nonbinding, while the U.S. administration has favored industry-led safeguards and Congress has yet to pass proposed federal requirements [17][1]. California’s transparency law took effect in January 2026; New York’s RAISE Act is due to take effect in January 2027, and Japan’s government aims to submit legislation requiring reports of serious AI failures to its 2027 ordinary parliamentary session [1][14]. At a Nov. 23 United Nations summit in Barbados, Finland’s Transport and Communications Minister Lulu Ranne said human interests and governance should be central to AI development [2]. Experts at a Brookings Institution discussion urged the United States and China to cooperate on incident reporting, testing standards and researcher exchanges, even if their domestic regulations differ [3]. In Russia, President Vladimir Putin called for clear limits on what AI agents can do without human approval [10]. AI safety expert Stuart Russell called for international standards and mandatory pre-release testing, while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that regulators should use existing laws unless they identify a specific gap [20][5]. Governments and AI leaders press for human oversight as safety rules diverge

Category: AI

Governments and technology leaders are pursuing AI safety measures ranging from voluntary international commitments to proposed inspections and mandatory incident reporting. The Paris Call, signed Nov. 9 by governments, AI companies and civil-society groups, is nonbinding, while the U.S. administration has favored industry-led safeguards and Congress has yet to pass proposed federal requirements [17][1]. California’s transparency law took effect in January 2026; New York’s RAISE Act is due to take effect in January 2027, and Japan’s government aims to submit legislation requiring reports of serious AI failures to its 2027 ordinary parliamentary session [1][14]. At a Nov. 23 United Nations summit in Barbados, Finland’s Transport and Communications Minister Lulu Ranne said human interests and governance should be central to AI development [2]. Experts at a Brookings Institution discussion urged the United States and China to cooperate on incident reporting, testing standards and researcher exchanges, even if their domestic regulations differ [3]. In Russia, President Vladimir Putin called for clear limits on what AI agents can do without human approval [10]. AI safety expert Stuart Russell called for international standards and mandatory pre-release testing, while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that regulators should use existing laws unless they identify a specific gap [20][5]. Japan’s proposed bill would allow inspections when safeguards are inadequate and penalties of up to 100 million yen, according to Nikkei [14].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We need to establish the limits of authority for AI agents - that is, the steps they cannot take without human oversight and participation.

— Vladimir Putin, President of Russia (TASS)

Did you know: The Paris Call’s initial signatory count was reported as six governments and 10 companies, but the Élysée list later cited in the article showed 19 governments and 11 companies [17].

Key Points

  • Paris commitments: The Paris Call includes commitments to independent validation, model fail-safes, ongoing risk assessments and faster sharing of information about serious incidents, but sets no deadlines [17].
  • Signatory gaps: China, Google and Meta were not listed at the time described [17].
  • Thailand’s legal gap: Technology law specialist Paiboon Amornpinyo said Thailand’s cybercrime, data-protection and cybersecurity laws were not designed for AI-driven attacks and called for an emergency decree while longer-term legislation is prepared [15].
  • Regulatory comparison: Russell said China had implemented tougher AI regulations than the United States and Europe [20].
  • Federal proposals: Congressional proposals include independent audits, incident reporting and pre-deployment evaluations, but none had become law [1].

Perspectives

Stuart Russell, University of California, Berkeley professor and AI expert: He warned that AI loss-of-control incidents already seen in cyberspace could eventually spill over into financial markets [20].

Sources: Hindustan Times

Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive: Huang urged data-center builders to work more closely with nearby communities, including making facilities more attractive and locating them far enough away to avoid disturbing residents [5].

Sources: NewsNation, republished by Yahoo

Kyle Chan, Brookings Institution fellow: He said discussions on human control of military AI could offer a practical area for gradual U.S.-China progress [3].

Sources: China Daily

Nobel Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes: Frydnes argued that accountability must remain with the people and governments that design, deploy and profit from AI, because a machine cannot answer to victims in court [7].

Sources: Rappler

Timeline

  • 9 November 2026: Governments, companies and civil-society groups signed the Paris Call [17].
  • 21 November 2026: Nobel Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes addressed AI accountability in Manila [7].
  • 23 November 2026: UN special summit on AI safety convened in Bridgetown, Barbados [2].
  • 26 November 2026: Japan’s proposed AI safety bill details were reported, targeting parliamentary submission in 2027 [14].

Industry Impact

  • Frontier AI developers: California’s law requires large developers to publish safety frameworks and report critical incidents; Illinois has introduced annual independent compliance audits beginning in 2028 [1].
  • AI services in Thailand: A technology law specialist warned that foreign-operated AI platforms and distributed computing infrastructure could complicate domestic data processing, oversight and sovereignty as AI services expand [15].
  • AI laboratories: The Paris Call recognizes the potential benefits of open-weight models for research, innovation and validation, while leaving unresolved how risks should be handled once weights are openly available [17].

Historical Background

The Paris Call drew on earlier international work, including the Hiroshima process, the Frontier Safety Commitments established at the Seoul AI Summit, the G7 Evian AI meeting and a United Nations Security Council AI session on Sept. 23, 2026 [17]. The Call also followed an appeal initiated by Finland and Norway for control of frontier AI models, which France later joined [17].

Business Angle

  • Federal proposals include independent audits, incident reporting and pre-deployment evaluations, though they have not become law [1].
  • Companies may need to limit AI systems’ permissions and establish ways to suspend or disable autonomous functions when necessary [1].
  • Connecticut has taken a narrower approach focused on internal risk-reporting mechanisms and whistleblower protections [1].

International Reactions

  • 🇫🇮 Finland: At the Nov. 23 summit, Ranne called for AI’s benefits to be shared more evenly [2].
  • 🇷🇺 Russia: Putin proposed updating the national AI strategy through 2036 and approving an action plan, arguing that people and autonomous systems should work together harmoniously [16].
  • 🇺🇸 United States: The U.S. government had not signed the Paris Call, although Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent attended the meeting, according to the signatory account [17].

Q&A

Q: What are the Paris Call’s main limitations?

A: A French civil-society signatory said the Call lacks common criteria for deciding whether models should be developed or deployed and does not guarantee sufficient access for validation bodies and governments. A common validation system has not yet been established [17].

Q: Would Japan’s proposal apply only to domestic AI companies?

A: No. The proposal also targets overseas developers of high-performance AI, according to Nikkei [14].

Action Items

  • Check whether frontier-AI rules apply to your organization’s AI use: Review the system developers, deployment locations and applicable state requirements, including California’s current law and New York’s upcoming RAISE Act [1].
  • Review AI vendor contracts for safety obligations: Check whether contracts cover incident notification, safety testing, human oversight and suspension or shutdown rights [1].

item.content:encoded:
Nvidia pauses AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian markets

Category: Technology

Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers containing its advanced artificial-intelligence chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported, citing three people familiar with the matter. The duration is unclear. The report described the hold as a compliance step while Nvidia and its partners work through new U.S. export controls [15][30][18]. The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule on Nov. 16 that took effect Nov. 19. It requires licenses for covered advanced-chip shipments to the four countries and Brazil. It also targets overseas data centers that provide substantial computing capacity to companies in China and other restricted jurisdictions. Existing providers serving those customers have 90 days to apply for licenses to continue those services [3][5][35]. The controls affect projects built around leasing Nvidia-powered computing to Chinese customers. Singapore cloud provider Aolani had planned to serve ByteDance; lenders have stopped extending about $500 million in credit for the project, and ByteDance may abandon the arrangement. Nvidia booked $104 billion through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, a figure that also includes some Taiwan and China revenue [15][42][13].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Key Points

  • Compute threshold: The rule requires a license when a data center supplies more than 12 million aggregate total processing performance units to covered customers; linked facilities count together [3][35][21].
  • U.S. carve-out: The destination-based licensing requirement does not apply to shipments for U.S.-headquartered companies or companies whose ultimate parent is U.S.-based, subject to reporting requirements [5][16][21].
  • Regional investment: Malaysia approved RM123.5 billion in data-center and cloud investments across 86 projects from January through September 2026, although the number relying on affected shipments is unknown [5].
  • Credit exposure: Lenders are also taking longer to review a $6.6 billion loan sought by Bain Capital’s Bridge Data Centres for Malaysian facilities serving ByteDance, according to CoinDesk [28].

Perspectives

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the Commerce Department’s rule is intended to block indirect access to restricted computing, including through smuggling routes and remote use of third-country data centers [38].

Sources: The Standard

Malaysia’s trade ministry said Malaysia does not require a local permit to import AI chips and does not enforce other countries’ unilateral export controls, but expects local businesses to take those rules into account [16].

Sources: News18

Regional cloud providers: Cloud operators have complained that the 90-day licensing period began without clear application instructions, making it harder to demonstrate compliance [6][15].

Sources: TechSpot

Timeline

  • 2022: United States restricted exports of advanced AI chips to China [4][35]
  • 16 November 2026: Commerce Department issued its interim rule on remote chip access [3][5]
  • 19 November 2026: New licensing requirements took effect for covered chip shipments [3][21]
  • 26 November 2026: Financial Times reported Nvidia’s shipment pause to four countries [15][18]
  • 18 January 2027: Public comment period on the interim rule is scheduled to close [35]

Technical Details

  • Remote-access threshold: The 12-million-unit trigger is roughly equivalent to the capacity of 750 Nvidia H100 or H200 chips [35].

Industry Impact

  • Data-center construction: Compliance checks could delay projects in Johor, Jakarta, Batam, Bangkok and Singapore; some regional AI clouds are also looking to AMD and newer suppliers as alternatives [10].

Historical Background

An October 2023 update targeted China-specific Nvidia chips, including the A800 and H800, as Washington sought to limit circumvention through third countries [35]. In May 2025, the Trump administration rescinded the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule before it took effect [3][6].

Q&A

Q: Does the reported shipment pause include Brazil?

A: Brazil is covered by the new licensing rule, but it was not named among the four countries in the reported shipment pause [5][16].

item.content:encoded:
X adds first parental controls for teens after safety scrutiny

Category: Technology

X introduced its first parental controls on Nov. 26 for users ages 13 to 17, giving parents and guardians tools to manage teens’ feeds, contacts and time spent on the social network [1][2][8]. Teen accounts default to protected mode, which restricts sensitive media and blocks targeted advertising. Adults can set daily usage limits, approve new followers, filter words, limit recommendations to accounts the teen follows and control who can send direct messages [4][7]. Supervision requires consent from both the adult and the teen. Parents can see weekly usage and which accounts their teen has messaged one-on-one, but cannot read the messages, view search or viewing histories, log in to the teen’s account or post on their behalf. Teenagers can see every change made [11][8]. One adult can supervise up to five teen accounts, while each teen account can be linked to only one adult. Supervision ends automatically when the teen turns 18 [2][9].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Parents want practical tools, and teens deserve room to grow. With Parental Controls on X, families can set the guardrails that fit their home, while teens keep ownership of their accounts and can see every change. Striking that balance is vital and what we set out to build.

— Michael O’Herlihy, head of safety at X (TechCrunch)

Key Points

  • Account linking: The parent starts setup in X’s settings and the teen completes it by scanning a QR code while logged into their account [5][11].
  • Age verification: X may verify a user’s age through a selfie check or identity document in some cases, but the platform has not specified when it will require either method [21].
  • Safety testing: The Center for Countering Digital Hate said two UK accounts posing as 13-year-olds could find sexual acts and pornographic images and videos on X [6].
  • Legal scrutiny: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general sued X and other Musk companies, alleging Grok helped spread non-consensual sexual images and child sexual abuse material [6][11].
  • Default account limits: Teen accounts are set so only approved followers can view posts and only accounts the teen follows can send direct messages [7].

Perspectives

X: The company says its platform is not designed or promoted for children, but says it takes extra care with young people who use it [12][1].

Sources: Gizmodo

Ofcom: The UK regulator’s investigation found that some age-gated pornography remained accessible to accounts not verified as belonging to adults. X subsequently changed its restrictions [6].

Sources: Digital Trends

Timeline

  • 2024: A study found nearly one-third of Gen Alpha children had X accounts [1]
  • September 2026: Ireland’s media watchdog opened an inquiry into X’s age checks [6]
  • 25 November 2026: X’s Safety account announced the parental-control tools [19]

Industry Impact

  • Social media safety features: X’s controls include feed recommendation limits and oversight of teen messaging contacts, features that Digital Trends says Instagram and TikTok had offered for some time [6].

Historical Background

X had operated for 20 years without parental controls for teen accounts [1].

International Reactions

  • 🇦🇺 Australia: Australia banned users under 16 from X in December 2025, according to TechJuice [7].
  • 🇬🇧 United Kingdom: The UK announced plans to include X in a proposed social-media ban for minors [7].

Q&A

Q: Can a teenager end supervision after agreeing to it?

A: Teens may request to end supervision, but the parent or guardian can approve or deny the request; supervision ends automatically at 18 [11][9].

Q: Does requiring approval for new followers change a teen account’s visibility?

item.content:encoded:
Analysts say GTA VI needs PC release to expand beyond console market

Category: Technology

Analysts estimate Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI sold 40.2 million to 47 million copies over its launch weekend, with several forecasting at least 50 million by year-end. The game, released Nov. 19, generated $3.79 billion on its first day, while Sony said more than 39 million people played it on PlayStation 5 during its first four days [1][17][19]. Analysts say console sales face a limited audience: Video-game market analyst Joost van Dreunen estimates about 137 million current-generation consoles are in use and says roughly one-quarter of that base bought the game before release. They identify a PC version, which has not been announced, as the main route to a larger market. Van Dreunen forecasts lifetime sales of 200 million to 250 million copies, while Enders Analysis’ Gareth Sutcliffe says reaching 100 million quickly would require more platforms [1]. Sony also reported 683 million hours played on PS5 from Nov. 19 through Nov. 22, an average of 17.4 hours per player. Near-term sales depend on holiday demand and console availability; analysts say Sony and Microsoft have limited ability to increase supply this quarter and in the first quarter [19][1].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Take-Two positioned GTA 6 less as a game and more as a blockbuster entertainment event.

— Joost van Dreunen, video-game market analyst (GamesIndustry.biz)

Key Points

  • Streaming audience: Streams Charts counted more than 420 million hours of GTA VI viewing across platforms in its first seven days, nearly three times the previous record held by Valorant’s 2020 closed beta [17].
  • Physical sales: Despite being sold in a box without a disc, the game generated £32 million in UK physical-retail revenue in three days, marking the country’s largest physical launch since 2019 [12].

Perspectives

Video-game market analysts: Enders Analysis’ Gareth Sutcliffe identifies support for more Apple-silicon iPhones and iPads from recent generations as a potential mobile expansion that could bring the game’s market to hundreds of millions of devices [1].

Sources: GamesIndustry.biz

Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain: The union says workers need a role in decisions affecting pay gaps, overtime rules, job security and the use of generative AI. It described the recognition ballot as a route to greater transparency [9].

Sources: Prachatai

Former Rockstar employees: Their lawyer argued that management had tolerated a private Discord server for years and acted only after union membership neared 10% of the workforce; Rockstar disputes that account [9].

Sources: Prachatai

Timeline

  • 12 November 2026: Rockstar employees’ union-recognition ballot opened [9]
  • 17 November 2026: Former employees’ lawyer delivered closing arguments in Scotland [9]
  • 19 November 2026: Grand Theft Auto VI launched for current-generation consoles [9][17]
  • 19–22 November 2026: Sony reported 39 million PS5 players and 683 million play hours for Nov. 19–22 [19]
  • 26 November 2026: Rockstar workers’ union-recognition ballot closed [9]

Technical Details

  • Xbox One cloud streaming: Digital Foundry found that the older Xbox One streams the Xbox Series S build rather than running GTA VI locally. The streamed image looked broadly similar, but frame pacing was less smooth [3].
  • PS5 power draw reports: A Polish console technician cited measurements of about 220 watts at the wall during light gameplay and 274.2 watts in a separate maximum-load test; no official finding linked those readings to reported console failures [6][19].

Industry Impact

  • Game platforms: Sony said GTA VI was the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles connected since the game’s launch. The release also set the platform’s concurrent-player record [19][17].
  • Retail formats: Estimates put physical sales in France above 1 million copies in the first three days, comparable to GTA V’s launch. In Spain, GTA VI had the largest physical launch in chart history [12].

Historical Background

Rockstar dismissed about 34 employees in the United Kingdom and Canada in October 2025, saying they had shared confidential company information in a Discord server; 23 former employees later brought a case alleging anti-union retaliation [9]. Researchers studying game-industry work practices have described “crunch” as sustained, heavy overtime and traced how it became normalized in the industry [9].

Business Angle

  • The launch could bolster Sony’s decision to end disc production from 2028, but physical formats still account for close to half of Nintendo’s first-party sales on Switch and Switch 2 [12].

Q&A

Q: When might the PC version arrive?

A: Joost van Dreunen says “next year is about PC,” but that is an analyst’s market outlook, not a Rockstar release announcement [1].

Q: What is the status of the Rockstar union ballot?

A: The recognition vote closed on Nov. 26 [9].

item.content:encoded:
1Password reports customer data theft; investigation continues

Category: Technology

Password manager 1Password says an attacker used a compromised employee GitHub account to access private source code, insert malicious code into backend services and download customer administrative records. The company began investigating on Nov. 19 and disclosed the incident on Nov. 25. Its investigation, assisted by independent cybersecurity experts, continues [3][12][16]. The stolen records included customer names, sign-in email addresses, account identifiers, activity timestamps, public keys and authentication parameters, as well as tokens in some invitation and recovery emails. The attacker also copied private source code and accessed the company’s software build-and-deployment system, which may hold infrastructure credentials. 1Password says the attacker did not access customer vault contents, passwords, recovery keys or the keys protecting vaults [3][5][13]. 1Password says exposed invitation and recovery tokens cannot be used alone to access accounts and reports no evidence of account takeovers. It disabled the compromised account, revoked a stolen token, rotated potentially exposed credentials and restored clean versions of affected services. The company has not disclosed the number of affected customers or how the attacker first accessed the employee’s GitHub account. It advises customers to watch for phishing messages [12][20][4].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

— 1Password (Help Net Security)

Key Points

  • Development controls: 1Password says it tightened protections for GitHub, its software build-and-deployment system and employee devices, and added tools to detect intrusions [5][12].
  • Customer notifications: 1Password said it individually notified a small number of people with outstanding provisioning or recovery invitations [5][12].
  • Company reach: 1Password serves millions of individual users and about 200,000 businesses, according to The Lec [16].
  • Phishing exposure: Names and email addresses linked to 1Password accounts could help scammers tailor fake recovery messages, a risk highlighted by the company and security coverage [6][13][9].

Perspectives

1Password: The company says the Secure Remote Password verifiers in the stolen records cannot authenticate users directly. Attempts to brute-force account passwords would also require Secret Keys, which 1Password says it does not store [3].

Sources: SecurityWeek

Sarkis Darbinyan, IT lawyer and digital-rights expert: Darbinyan said customer metadata can reveal who uses a service and when they were active, a concern for journalists and activists. He identified phishing as the immediate concern [25].

Sources: Novaya Gazeta Europe

Timeline

  • 2022: LastPass disclosed a breach that later exposed encrypted customer vault copies [7]
  • October 2023: 1Password disclosed an Okta-linked security incident without customer data exposure [8]
  • June 2026: LastPass reported another breach exposing customer information, not saved passwords [8][20]
  • 19 November 2026: 1Password began investigating suspicious access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account [12][16]
  • 25 November 2026: 1Password publicly disclosed the incident and warned customers about phishing [4][13]

Technical Details

  • Public keys: The exposed keys are public by design, and 1Password says their disclosure does not affect account security [12][4].
  • Invitation tokens: Tokens taken from some invitation, provisioning and recovery emails require an additional single sign-on login or email verification code; 1Password lengthened that code to 10 alphanumeric characters [5][12].

Historical Background

LastPass’s 2022 breach began with a development-environment compromise; information stolen then helped attackers in a later intrusion that exposed encrypted vault backups. The UK Information Commission’s Office later fined LastPass £1.2 million over the incident [7][25].

Q&A

Q: Does 1Password recommend that users change their account passwords?

A: No. The company says customers do not need to change their account passwords or Secret Keys, but should be alert to unsolicited phishing attempts [3][13].

Q: Could the breach disrupt use of the service?

A: 1Password said the incident did not affect its services, availability or product security, and that its apps and browser extensions were unaffected [5][3].

Action Items

  • Verify unexpected 1Password messages through the official service: Do not follow links or act on requests in unexpected emails, texts or calls about invitations or account recovery. Open the official app or type the company’s website address yourself [4][13].
  • Do not disclose account secrets: 1Password says it will never ask for an account password or Secret Key; enter those only in the official app or website [4].

item.title: Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian defense technicians
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (World / Gulf Security)
item.description: Two Italian technicians were killed when drones struck a Kuwaiti military facility on Thursday, Nov. 26, and falling debris injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, Kuwaiti and Italian officials said [7][20][2]. The men worked for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian unit of German defense contractor Rheinmetall, maintaining detection antennas for Kuwait’s Skyguard air-defense system [12][19]. Kuwait and Italy blamed Iran; Tehran denied responsibility. Iran’s armed forces said they had conducted no operation in the region, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi offered to join Kuwait and Italy in investigating the incident [3][18]. Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian defense technicians

Category: World

Two Italian technicians were killed when drones struck a Kuwaiti military facility on Thursday, Nov. 26, and falling debris injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, Kuwaiti and Italian officials said [7][20][2]. The men worked for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian unit of German defense contractor Rheinmetall, maintaining detection antennas for Kuwait’s Skyguard air-defense system [12][19]. Kuwait and Italy blamed Iran; Tehran denied responsibility. Iran’s armed forces said they had conducted no operation in the region, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi offered to join Kuwait and Italy in investigating the incident [3][18]. Kuwait said its forces detected and intercepted hostile drones, but the defense ministry did not identify the facility or describe the damage [20][52]. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the drones were Iranian-made and noted that Iran-aligned armed groups also operate in the region [20]. Attacks on Gulf states hosting U.S. forces had resumed after a relative lull, while negotiations to end the U.S.-Iran war remained stalled [7][41]. Kuwait condemned the attack as a violation of its sovereignty and said it reserved the right to take measures to defend its territory [42]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged increased pressure on Tehran, while Araghchi proposed a joint investigation with Kuwait and Italy [3][59].

Trump urges Putin to halt European aggression as Ukraine war intensifies

Category: World

President Donald Trump said on Nov. 26 that he had urged Russian President Vladimir Putin during talks in China the previous week to pull back “all military aggression” across Europe. He said he hoped that could lead to a quick deal to end the war in Ukraine but did not specify which territories or actions he meant. His statement followed a Florida meeting with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, after which they called on Russia and Ukraine to avoid steps that could widen the war [1][4][5]. At their China meeting, Trump greeted Putin as a “friend,” worrying officials in Kyiv and European capitals. Russian strikes hit Kyiv overnight, wounding seven people, while Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, warned of another possible mass attack. European concern has also grown after missiles landed in Poland [4][9][7]. Washington has delayed a review of the U.S. military presence in Europe beyond its provisional Dec. 1 deadline while it assesses options and European offers to replace some U.S. capabilities. The review will go to Trump, but officials have not set a date for a decision [3].

Primary Source: View original article

The biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other

— President Donald Trump (Daily Maverick)

Key Points

  • Troop review: The review covers U.S. troop levels, bases and overflight rights; about 80,000 U.S. troops are stationed in Europe, and the Pentagon is preparing five options [3].
  • Baltic tensions: Estonia accused Russian security services of ordering an attempted arson attack on a defense company; Moscow denied involvement [7].
  • War’s reach: Ukraine said its drones struck Russian oil facilities and an airfield, while Ukraine’s prime minister said Russian attacks hit two foreign grain ships carrying more than 100,000 tonnes [9][17].
  • EU financing: EU leaders debated a proposed €45 billion loan to meet Ukraine’s needs in 2027; European Council President António Costa said 24 member states supported it [9].
  • Territorial deadlock: Trump envoy Jared Kushner said territory in eastern Ukraine claimed by Moscow remained a sticking point in discussions [6][2].

Perspectives

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy: He said Ukraine would rebuild what Russia strikes and retaliate against every Russian attack, while urging Ukrainians to heed missile alerts [9].

Sources: Al Jazeera

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov: He rejected the suggestion that Moscow was widening the conflict, blaming Kyiv for attempts to expand its geographical scope [30].

Sources: The Kyiv Independent

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte: He said American leadership remained essential as NATO sought to build a stronger Europe within the alliance [7].

Sources: TIME

Trump envoy Jared Kushner: He described Putin as having shown restraint by not using nuclear weapons and warned that miscalculation could escalate the war [6][2].

Sources: The Hindu

Timeline

  • February 2022: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine [6].
  • 19 November 2026: Trump and Putin met in Shenzhen alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping [31][30].
  • 25 November 2026: Trump and Rutte issued a joint call against expanding the war [4][6].
  • 26 November 2026: Trump publicly disclosed his appeal to Putin for restraint [1][2].
  • 26 November 2026: Washington delayed release of its Europe force-posture review beyond the provisional Dec. 1 deadline [3].

Historical Background

Trump has spoken of negotiating an end to the war since taking office in January 2025, but no peace agreement has been reached [32][22]. In October, he agreed with Putin on Russian diesel deliveries to the United States, easing economic pressure on Moscow amid rising fuel prices [22].

Humanitarian Impact

Crews were working to restore electricity in six Ukrainian regions after Russia launched ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight [5].

Q&A

Q: Has Putin said whether he will attend the G20 meeting in Florida?

A: No. Trump said Putin would be welcome at the Dec. 14–15 summit, but the Kremlin said no decision had been made on his attendance [15][16].

item.content:encoded:
EU leaders fail to agree on €1.78 trillion seven-year budget

Category: World

European Union leaders ended a Brussels summit early on Nov. 26 without agreement on the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget, a proposed €1.78 trillion package already cut by about €204 billion from the European Commission’s initial plan. European Council President António Costa said governments remained divided over the budget’s total size, spending allocations and new sources of EU revenue. The second day of talks was cancelled [7][5][12]. Germany and other net contributors want deeper cuts and more spending on defense and competitiveness, while France, Italy and other governments focused on cohesion funding oppose reductions to farm support and regional development. The dispute also became linked to a proposed €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027: 24 member states backed it, Bulgaria said it would fund only the non-military portion, and Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia remained opposed [64][17][16]. Leaders are due to resume negotiations at a summit on Dec. 17-18, aiming to reach agreement by year-end. The budget requires unanimous approval, and French President Emmanuel Macron has warned that without a deal by Dec. 31, formal talks would have to wait until after France’s 2027 presidential election [64][63][29].

Europe needs solid finances. We can’t and we mustn’t take on more debt.

— German Chancellor Friedrich Merz (South China Morning Post)

Key Points

  • Budget priorities: Agriculture and cohesion policy each account for about one-third of the EU budget, while the proposed package would devote roughly €740 billion to farmers and poorer regions [4][64].
  • Ukraine allocation: The proposed €45 billion loan divides into €20 billion for civilian needs and €25 billion for arms and ammunition; the 2028-2034 draft also includes up to €100 billion for Ukraine [2][26].
  • New revenue: A proposed digital-services levy could raise €35 billion, but Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin said it conflicted with efforts to improve European competitiveness [9][61].
  • ECB appointment: Leaders separately backed Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos, former Bank of Spain governor, to succeed Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president in February [19][20].
  • Pandemic debt: The current budget proposal includes €140 billion to repay borrowing undertaken during the pandemic [64].

Perspectives

European Council President António Costa: Costa said the summit was a necessary step and stressed that the EU needed a new budget in place from Jan. 1, 2028.

Sources: Euronews

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and net-contributor governments: Merz threatened to block the budget unless all 27 members backed the separate Ukraine loan, arguing the bloc should share the cost of aid [15][16].

Sources: The Straits Times, The Guardian

French President Emmanuel Macron: Macron called the proposed reductions a strategic error, warning they could leave Europe lagging in investment behind China and the United States [66].

Sources: Sud Ouest

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin: Martin identified the Common Agricultural Policy as a priority, saying it is a key EU funding stream for Ireland’s agriculture and food industry [61].

Sources: TheJournal.ie

Timeline

  • 16 July 2025: The European Commission published its initial 2028-2034 budget proposal [46]
  • 26 November 2026: Leaders ended the Brussels summit without agreement and cancelled Friday’s talks [12][14]
  • 17 December 2026: EU leaders are scheduled to resume budget negotiations in Brussels [1][64]

Industry Impact

  • Defense and security: The draft would more than triple defense funding in real terms and set aside €15.6 billion for routes to move troops and military equipment across the bloc [3].
  • Ukraine financing: The EU would borrow against its current budget, which expires at the end of 2027, to fund the proposed 2027 loan. The loan would be repaid only when Russia pays war reparations [63][64].

Historical Background

The EU’s budget framework is traditionally set for seven-year periods and has required unanimous approval by the European Council since the 2009 Lisbon Treaty [46]. The current 2021-2027 framework was agreed on Dec. 10-11, 2020, with the full set of financial acts published on Dec. 22, only nine days before it took effect [46].

item.title: New Zealand coalition loses majority; centrist party holds balance of power
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (World / Elections)
item.description: New Zealand’s governing National-led coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the final count of the Nov. 7 election, leaving it with 65 seats in a 130-seat Parliament, one short of the number needed to govern without additional support. The centrist Opportunity Party, which won seven seats, now holds the balance of power. The opposition Labour-led bloc has 58 seats and cannot form a majority even with Opportunity’s support [2][5][4]. The Electoral Commission’s count included 484,865 special votes cast overseas or outside voters’ electorates. National lost two seats compared with the preliminary tally; Labour gained two electorate seats and the Greens one. Prime Minister and National leader Christopher Luxon, who had ruled out working with Opportunity during the campaign, said formal talks would begin with his existing partners and Opportunity. Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong said her support depends on policy commitments and that she will not back a government with New Zealand First leader Winston Peters as foreign affairs minister [2][5][6]. Negotiations could extend into 2027. Luxon has warned that talks may be difficult, and failure to secure a governing or confidence-and-supply arrangement could lead to another election. A recount could still change the seat totals: applications are due by Dec. 3, and a recount could take a further five days [2][12].

New Zealand coalition loses majority; centrist party holds balance of power

Category: World

New Zealand’s governing National-led coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the final count of the Nov. 7 election, leaving it with 65 seats in a 130-seat Parliament, one short of the number needed to govern without additional support. The centrist Opportunity Party, which won seven seats, now holds the balance of power. The opposition Labour-led bloc has 58 seats and cannot form a majority even with Opportunity’s support [2][5][4]. The Electoral Commission’s count included 484,865 special votes cast overseas or outside voters’ electorates. National lost two seats compared with the preliminary tally; Labour gained two electorate seats and the Greens one. Prime Minister and National leader Christopher Luxon, who had ruled out working with Opportunity during the campaign, said formal talks would begin with his existing partners and Opportunity. Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong said her support depends on policy commitments and that she will not back a government with New Zealand First leader Winston Peters as foreign affairs minister [2][5][6]. Negotiations could extend into 2027. Luxon has warned that talks may be difficult, and failure to secure a governing or confidence-and-supply arrangement could lead to another election. A recount could still change the seat totals: applications are due by Dec. 3, and a recount could take a further five days [2][12].

item.content:encoded:
Spain votes Sunday with far-right Vox poised for national government role

Category: World

Spain votes on Nov. 29 in a snap parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s eight years in office and give far-right Vox its first role in a national government since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship ended in 1975. Pre-election polls put the conservative People’s Party (PP) near 31%, the Socialists (PSOE) around 29% to 30% and Vox at roughly 17% to 18%. The PP is expected to need Vox’s support to reach the 176 seats required for a majority in the 350-seat Congress [3][9][13]. Sánchez called the early vote after parliament rejected housing measures on Oct. 2, amid anger over high rents and evictions. The campaign has also focused on corruption investigations involving people close to Sánchez, two fatal train crashes and migration, including the summer influx into the North African enclave of Ceuta [3][5][6]. The PP and Vox have signaled changes to climate policy. Polling stations open at 9 a.m. local time and close at 8 p.m. If no bloc secures a majority, parties will have to negotiate support for a government [13][10][15].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

A government of the PP that includes Vox would not be just another government; it would mean an enormous step backwards. It would mean rolling back the clock 40, 50 years

— Pedro Sánchez, prime minister of Spain (The Associated Press)

Key Points

  • Youth support: Support for Vox has risen to 23.2% among voters aged 18 to 24, slightly above the Socialists’ 22%, according to Spain’s November polling [17].
  • Housing pledges: PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has promised one million new homes over four years, while Sánchez has emphasized tighter housing-market regulation and restrictions on unauthorized tourist rentals [5].
  • Rail scrutiny: After two deadly train crashes this year, Feijóo has pledged a rapid audit of the rail network if elected; the transport minister resigned after the second crash [5][13].
  • Election mechanics: Voters choose party lists in 52 constituencies, and parties need at least 3% of a constituency’s vote to qualify for seats there [13].
  • Coalition tensions: The PP and Vox have governed together in four regions, where they have clashed over policy [27][42].

Perspectives

Pedro Sánchez, prime minister of Spain: Sánchez has defended legal immigration, arguing that people who come to Spain bring economic and social benefits [5].

Sources: The Associated Press

Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of the conservative People’s Party: Feijóo has made competent administration central to his campaign, casting himself as a manager who would restore the quality of public services [5].

Sources: The Associated Press

Vox, Spain’s far-right party: Vox advocates giving Spaniards priority in access to public services and benefits, and calls for mass deportations and tougher immigration controls [9][10].

Sources: The Associated Press

Javier Carbonell, European Policy Centre policy analyst: Carbonell said many people remain angry despite Spain’s strong economic growth because they face a housing crisis and inflation. He warned that voters could also turn against a PP-Vox government [14].

Sources: FRANCE 24

Timeline

  • 2 October 2026: Parliament rejected two emergency housing decrees from Sánchez’s minority government [3].
  • 5 October 2026: Sánchez announced an early election after the housing-decree defeat [12].
  • 11 November 2026: Unions held a nationwide general strike over housing costs and wages [28][25].
  • 23 November 2026: Spain released the final pre-election polls permitted under election law [21][34].
  • 29 November 2026: Voters elect a new Congress and most members of the Senate [13].

Historical Background

Vox was founded in 2013 by former members of the PP’s more hard-line wing. Its breakthrough came after the 2017 Catalan independence referendum: it entered Andalusia’s regional parliament in 2018 and won 52 seats in Spain’s national parliament in a repeat election in November 2019 [35].

Q&A

Q: Would Vox necessarily take cabinet seats if the PP wins?

A: No. Feijóo has indicated he would prefer a minority government with Vox’s parliamentary backing, but has not ruled out a coalition arrangement like the PP-Vox government in Andalusia [38].

Defence minister probes claim nurse was threatened over Poilievre photo

Category: Canada

Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty says he is trying to resolve a dispute involving government contractor Calian Health after Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre alleged a nurse’s contract was at risk because she spoke with him at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright. Maureen Carpenter, who works at the Wainwright hospital under contract with Calian, met Poilievre after an Oct. 17 fire at the Alberta base that killed five soldiers and injured 39 people, 19 critically [1][2][5]. Poilievre raised a point of privilege in the House of Commons on Wednesday, saying the alleged employment consequences interfered with his work as Carpenter’s MP. McGuinty said he asked his deputy minister to raise the matter with Calian but cannot intervene directly in a private contract. He has spoken with Carpenter’s brother, but not with Carpenter. Calian had not responded to media requests for comment. The House Speaker is expected to rule on Poilievre’s privilege claim [6][7][1].

  • Meeting permission: Poilievre said Carpenter spoke with him on base with permission from the unit commander, and that he had permission from the base commander to visit [6][9].

item.title: Doctors warn Wainwright fire injuries may require years of recovery
item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Canada / Military)
item.description: Nearly six weeks after a wind-driven grass fire burned soldiers during a training exercise at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, doctors say some face months or years of physical and psychological recovery [2][3][4]. item.content:encoded:
Global temperatures exceed pre-industrial average by 2°C for a week as El Niño intensifies

Category: Science

Preliminary data from Copernicus, the European Union’s climate-monitoring service, show global temperatures stayed more than 2°C above the 1850–1900 average for seven consecutive days, reaching 2.25°C above that baseline on Monday [1]. These daily readings do not establish that the Paris Agreement’s temperature limit has been breached: that target is assessed over at least 20 years [1]. Scientists attribute the spike to long-term human-caused warming combined with a strong El Niño [1][5]. The record run coincided with COP31 climate negotiations in Turkey, where nearly 200 countries failed to agree on language about moving away from fossil fuels [1]. The UK Met Office forecasts an unusually sharp rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide in 2027 as drought weakens natural carbon sinks; one estimate puts the year-to-year increase at about 3.5 parts per million [1][3]. The current El Niño began in June and is expected to continue until at least March [1].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

El Niño will come and go; the underlying warming from greenhouse gas emissions will not, unless we bring those emissions down.

— Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for Climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (Financial Times)

Key Points

  • Autumn records: October 2026 was the warmest October worldwide since records began, while Toronto set an October heat record dating back 80 years [2].
  • Pacific conditions: The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration put the chance of a historic El Niño event by January at 60% [1].
  • Coastal hazards: Storms prompted flood warnings along the California coast and as far north as Oregon and Washington; New York postponed its Thanksgiving Day parade until Saturday [1].
  • Emissions trajectory: A climate researcher writing for The Conversation said global emissions may have peaked in 2026, but stressed that a peak does not amount to the steep cuts needed to reduce warming [5].

Perspectives

Samantha Burgess, climate strategic lead at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, said governments face two tasks: preparing communities for higher temperatures and accelerating cuts in greenhouse gas emissions. She cited heat-related damage to roads and railways and pressure on hospitals [3].

Sources: Știrile Pro TV

Richard Betts, head of climate impacts research at the Met Office Hadley Centre, warned that drought in regions such as the Amazon can increase wildfire risks, harm ecosystems and threaten food and water supplies [3].

Sources: Știrile Pro TV

Timeline

  • 2015: Nearly 200 countries signed the Paris climate agreement [3]
  • 17 November 2023: Global daily temperatures first exceeded 2°C above pre-industrial levels [1]
  • February 2024: A second brief period exceeded the 2°C threshold [3]
  • 23 November 2026: Daily temperature anomaly reached 2.24°C, according to Copernicus data [4]

Technical Details

  • El Niño signal: Sea-surface temperatures more than 4°C above average across the eastern equatorial Pacific reflect the event’s exceptional strength. The warm water affects global average temperatures [1][5].

Scientific Significance

  • Scale of the drivers: El Niño events can raise global average temperatures by tenths of a degree, while cumulative human emissions have warmed the planet by almost 1.5°C [5].
  • Regional heat risks: Major El Niño events increase the chance of heat in Australia and Indonesia, and this event is expected to bring particularly humid, dangerous heat to the tropics [5][1].

Historical Background

The 2015 Paris Agreement set a goal of limiting global warming to 1.5°C and keeping it well below 2°C compared with pre-industrial levels [1][3].

Q&A

Q: How unusual is the forecast rise in carbon dioxide?

A: The forecast year-to-year increase is about one-third faster than in recent years and nearly twice the rate consistent with limiting warming to 1.5°C [3].

Q: When might the current El Niño’s effects be most pronounced?

A: The event is forecast to peak between November and January, but scientists expect some of its effects to be felt several months after the peak [3].

item.content:encoded:
Researchers identify possible largest known scorpion, over one meter long

Category: Science

Researchers have identified Praearcturus gigas, a scorpion known from a fossil found in the United Kingdom dating to about 415 million years ago, as a candidate for the largest known scorpion. They estimated that the animal exceeded one meter in length. A new analysis combining CT scans with traditional fossil tracings resolved decades of uncertainty over its classification [1][2][4]. Paleontologist Richie Howard and colleagues infer that it hunted both on land and in water; terrestrial ecosystems were still developing at the time [1][3]. The researchers suggest that the absence of other large predators may have enabled its large size, while later competition may have contributed to its decline [1][4].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

If this is the case, then Praearcturus is an example of an animal that likely returned to the water after its ancestors moved onto land.

— Greg Edgecombe, paleontologist at the Natural History Museum in the UK (ScienceAlert)

Key Points

  • Large pincers: Its pincers measured about 16 centimeters, longer than the bodies of many scorpion species alive today [1][4].
  • Possible sound: Ridge patterns on a limb may indicate stridulation—sound production by rubbing body parts together, a behavior used by some modern scorpions [1][2].
  • Fossil comparison: The team compared the British fossils with Canadian specimens of the ancient scorpion Eramoscorpius to place P. gigas within the scorpion family tree [1][4].

Technical Details

  • Aquatic adaptation: Fossils from Wales preserve flap-like epimera resembling structures in lobsters and crabs. Researchers cite these features as evidence that P. gigas could forage in water as well as on land [1][2].
